events.text: {npc} is on the same ferry as you, and halfway across the brown river {he} starts to sing a boatman's song under {his} breath, and gets the words wrong. The old ferryman winces at every wrong word.

choices.text: Sing the right words along

mem.note: sang on the ferry with me

effects.log: The ferryman joins in, then the passengers. The whole ferry lands singing. {npc} grins at you all the way up the bank.

choices.text: Ask the ferryman for the true song

mem.note: learned the ferry song with me

effects.log: The ferryman sings it properly, all nine verses, in a cracked old voice. {npc} writes the words on {his} sleeve in charcoal.

events.text: {npc} finds you in the market with news: the old ferryman has retired, and the new one does not know the song. {npc} thinks this is a disaster and has a plan.

choices.text: Teach the new ferryman together

mem.note: taught the ferry song with me

effects.log: The new ferryman is a shy young person who learns quickly. On the first crossing with the song, the old ferryman is on the bank, listening.

choices.text: Write the song down and nail it in the ferry

mem.note: nailed the song to the ferry

effects.log: Nine verses, nailed to the ferry rail. Passengers read it and sing. The ferry is the loudest boat on the river.

events.text: Years later, crossing the river, you hear the ferry song before you see the boat. It is {npc}, grey now, leading the singing, still getting one word wrong, on purpose.

choices.text: Sing the wrong word with {npc}

mem.note: sang the wrong word with me

effects.log: You both sing it wrong, loudly. The young ferryman laughs and corrects you, and you both ignore it.

choices.text: Sit and listen to the whole crossing

effects.log: {npc} sings all nine verses for you, the right way. On the far bank {he} says it was the first time {he} ever got them all right.

events.text: {npc} comes to you with a ledger and a frown. A shopkeeper says {npc} owes three times what {he} borrowed. {npc} cannot read the shopkeeper's figures and suspects a trick.

choices.text: Go through the ledger line by line

mem.note: found the trick in the ledger

ok.log: The shopkeeper has added the interest twice and the date wrongly. You show it, line by line, in front of the whole shop. The debt shrinks by two thirds.

fail.log: You find one mistake, but not the rest. The debt shrinks a little. {npc} is grateful anyway, and starts learning figures.

choices.text: Lend {npc} the money to clear it (10 taels)

effects.log: {npc} pays the shopkeeper and swears to pay you back. The shopkeeper looks disappointed, which tells you everything.

events.text: {npc} has been learning figures since the ledger, at night, with a borrowed abacus, and now keeps the accounts for half the street. {He} wants you to check {his} first big job.

choices.text: Check it all, carefully

effects.log: It is perfect. {npc} pretends to have known that, and then has to sit down.

choices.text: Plant a deliberate mistake to see if {he} catches it

effects.log: {npc} catches it in a breath and looks at you with deep suspicion, then laughs.

events.text: {npc} keeps the accounts for the whole market now, honestly, and the market is better for it. {He} comes to you with a gift: a small abacus of black wood.

choices.text: Accept it

effects.log: It sits on your table. Every time you use it, it clicks like a small applause.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to teach the street's children with it

effects.log: {npc} sets up a little class in the market on rest days. Nobody in that street is cheated by a ledger again.

events.arc: The One Who Walks at Night
events.text: {npc} cannot sleep and walks the town at night, and tonight {he} knocks on your shutter, seeing your lamp, and asks if you want to walk too.

choices.text: Walk with {npc}

mem.note: walked the night town with me

effects.log: You walk past the shut shops, the sleeping dogs, the night watchman snoring at the post. {npc} knows every cat by name. It is a different town at night.

choices.text: Invite {npc} in for tea instead

mem.note: let me sleep in their chair

effects.log: You talk until the lamp oil runs out. {npc} falls asleep in your chair, mid-sentence, for the first time in weeks.

events.arc: The One Who Walks at Night
events.text: Walking the night town with {npc} again, you find a fire just starting in a baker's chimney, with everyone asleep inside.

choices.text: Climb up and smother it

mem.note: put out the fire with me

ok.log: You climb the roof and stuff the chimney with wet sacks. The baker comes out in a nightshirt and gives you both a year of bread.

mem.note: burned a hand saving the bakery

fail.log: You burn your hand, but the fire goes out. The baker's household is saved, and very grateful, and puts salve on your hand.

choices.text: Bang on every door and wake the street

effects.log: The whole street turns out with buckets. The fire is out in moments. {npc} says night walking has finally been useful.

events.arc: The One Who Walks at Night
events.text: {npc} sleeps at night now, mostly. But once a year, on the night of the bakery fire, {he} knocks on your shutter and you walk the town together, past the cats and the sleeping watchman.

choices.text: Walk until dawn

effects.log: At dawn the baker leaves a loaf on the step, as every year. You share it on the bridge.

choices.text: Bring along someone else who cannot sleep

effects.log: A young clerk who has been pacing at night. The three of you walk the town. {npc} names every cat for the newcomer.

events.text: {npc} has watched you eat cold rice standing up one too many times. {He} arrives with a cleaver, an onion and a stern face. 'You are going to learn one dish,' {he} says. 'One.'

choices.text: Learn the dish

effects.log: Egg and tomato over rice. You cut your finger, burn the egg and cry over the onion. The dish is edible. {npc} says it is a start.

choices.text: Insist on learning three

effects.log: {npc} looks at you with new respect and teaches you three. All of them are egg-based. You eat eggs for a month.

events.text: {npc} returns to inspect. You have made the egg dish two hundred times. {He} tastes it and says nothing, then takes out a fish.

choices.text: Learn the fish

effects.log: Ginger, spring onion, hot oil poured over at the end so it sings. Your fish sings on the third try. {npc} closes {his} eyes.

choices.text: Cook the egg dish for {npc} instead

effects.log: You cook it for {npc}, perfectly, with a flourish. {npc} eats it slowly and says it is better than {his} own, and is lying, and it is the nicest lie.

events.text: {npc} is ill and cannot cook, and has been eating cold rice standing up. You arrive with a cleaver, an onion and a stern face.

choices.text: Cook every dish {npc} taught you

effects.log: Egg and tomato, the singing fish, a soup you invented. {npc} eats at the table and laughs at the stern face, and gets well.

choices.text: Teach {npc}'s neighbour's child the egg dish

mem.note: taught someone to cook for me

effects.log: Now somebody will cook for {npc} every day. The child is very serious about it. {npc} says it is the circle closing.

events.text: {npc} has been feeding a stray dog behind the noodle stalls and wants your help: the dog is hurt in one leg, and {npc} is afraid of it.

choices.text: Splint the leg together

effects.log: The dog lets you do it, trembling. {npc} holds its head and talks nonsense to it the whole time. The leg heals crooked and strong.

choices.text: Pay a horse doctor (3 taels)

effects.log: The horse doctor laughs at being called for a dog, then does a fine job. {npc} names the dog after the horse doctor, who is flattered.

events.text: The crooked-legged dog follows {npc} everywhere now, and you, when you are together. Today it has dragged a purse out of the canal, heavy with silver, and dropped it at your feet.

choices.text: Find the owner

effects.log: The purse belongs to a tea merchant who weeps and gives the dog a whole roast duck. The dog is famous in the market.

choices.text: Hand it to the magistrate's clerk

mem.note: went to the clerk with me

effects.log: The clerk counts it, writes it down and, astonishingly, finds the owner. The dog gets a mention in the court record, which {npc} copies out and frames.

events.text: The crooked-legged dog is old, and white in the face, and sleeps in the sun by the noodle stalls where {npc} first fed it. {npc} sits with it every afternoon.

choices.text: Sit with them both

effects.log: The dog puts its head on your foot. {npc} says it has never done that for anyone but {him}.

choices.text: Bring the dog a roast duck, for the purse

mem.note: brought the old dog a duck

effects.log: The dog eats it slowly and with great dignity. The noodle sellers applaud.

events.text: {npc} has seen your handwriting on a shop sign and has decided that {his} is better. {He} challenges you to a contest of characters in the temple courtyard, the monks to judge.

choices.text: Accept and write your best

ok.log: The monks give it to you, narrowly. {npc} bows, examines your brushwork for an hour, and asks to try again next year.

fail.log: The monks give it to {npc}, narrowly. {npc} is so pleased {he} buys you a new brush.

choices.text: Suggest you write one scroll together instead

effects.log: {npc} is baffled, then intrigued. You write alternate lines of one poem. The monks hang it in the hall.

events.text: The contest has become a yearly event, and the temple courtyard fills with spectators. This year {npc} has a sprained wrist and will not withdraw.

choices.text: Write with your other hand, to be fair

effects.log: Both of you write terribly. The crowd adores it. The monks declare a draw and serve everyone tea.

choices.text: Win, and then mind {npc}'s wrist

effects.log: You win. Then you bind the wrist and grind {npc}'s ink for a month. {npc} says this is a dishonour and is very grateful.

events.text: The temple has asked you and {npc} to write the new board over its gate, together, after all these years of contests. Four characters, very large.

choices.text: Write two each

mem.note: wrote the temple gate with me

effects.log: Two in your hand, two in {npc}'s. You can tell exactly which are whose. The monks say that is the point.

choices.text: Let {npc} write all four

effects.log: {npc} writes them, and they are the best characters {he} has ever made, and {he} knows you know.

events.arc: The Letter in the Wrong House
events.text: {npc} brings you a letter that came to {his} house by mistake. It is addressed to someone who lived in your house forty years ago, and it has been on the road, the seals say, for nine years.

choices.text: Open it to find the family

mem.note: opened the old letter with me

effects.log: It is from a soldier at the frontier, to a mother, saying the writer is alive. The mother's name is on it. You and {npc} decide to find the family.

choices.text: Ask the oldest neighbour

mem.note: asked about the old letter with me

effects.log: The oldest neighbour remembers the family: they moved to the next town. {npc} offers to carry it there with you.

events.arc: The Letter in the Wrong House
events.text: You and {npc} walk to the next town with the nine-year letter. The mother is long gone, but the son is alive, grey and puzzled, at the door. It is the soldier who wrote it.

choices.text: Give it to the old soldier

effects.log: The old soldier reads that old letter, sent to a mother, nine years on the road. The soldier laughs and cries and invites you both in.

choices.text: Read it aloud for the old soldier, whose eyes are bad

mem.note: read the letter aloud with me

effects.log: You read it aloud. The old soldier listens to a young self promise to come home, and says, 'I did.'

events.arc: The Letter in the Wrong House
events.text: A letter comes to your house, and this one is for you, from the old soldier in the next town. It says, in a careful hand: thank you, and come for New Year. {npc} has the same letter.

choices.text: Go together for New Year

mem.note: went to the soldier's New Year with me

effects.log: The old soldier's house is full of grandchildren who have heard the story. You and {npc} are given the best seats.

choices.text: Write back, and send it the slow way

mem.note: sent the letter the slow way

effects.log: You send it by the slowest post. {npc} laughs at you. It arrives in nine days, which disappoints you both.

events.text: It is pouring, and {npc} hands you an oiled-paper umbrella in the street. 'Bring it back whenever,' {he} says, and runs off with a cloth over {his} head.

choices.text: Bring it back the next day

effects.log: {npc}'s door has a rack of twelve umbrellas, all lent out once and come back. {npc} is pleased to have the thirteenth home.

choices.text: Bring it back with a new one beside it (2 taels)

effects.log: {npc} puts the new umbrella on the rack. 'Now there are two to lend,' {he} says, as if you had planted a tree.

events.text: In a sudden storm {npc} is caught out with no umbrella, every one of {his} umbrellas lent. {npc} is standing under a dripping eave, laughing at the irony.

choices.text: Hold your umbrella over {npc} all the way home

mem.note: lent me an umbrella at last

effects.log: You walk {npc} home under one umbrella, both half wet. {npc} says it is the first time {he} has been lent one.

choices.text: Run and fetch umbrellas from the lent ones

effects.log: You knock on three doors. All three people have {npc}'s umbrellas and come out with them at once. {npc} is surrounded by umbrellas.

events.text: {npc}'s umbrella rack has spread: half the shops in the street keep one now, by the door, for anyone. {npc} is old, and very proud of it, and asks you to keep {his} rack going.

choices.text: Take {npc}'s rack to your door

effects.log: Twelve umbrellas by your door. Within a month, nine are lent. They all come back.

choices.text: Paint each umbrella with {npc}'s name

mem.note: painted my name on the umbrellas

effects.log: Every umbrella in the street now carries {npc}'s name, small, by the handle. People who borrow them ask who {npc} is.

events.text: {npc} has been apprenticed to a carpenter and has made a chair, the first thing {he} has ever made alone. It wobbles. {He} wants you to have it, and is very red about it.

choices.text: Take it and use it every day

effects.log: You put a folded paper under one leg. The chair does not wobble. You sit in it every day, and {npc} notices.

choices.text: Help {npc} find the wobble

effects.log: One leg is a hair short. You find it together. {npc} trims the other three and the chair is now a hair shorter and perfect.

events.text: {npc} has made a table to go with the chair. It does not wobble at all. {He} watches you sit at it as if the table might bite.

choices.text: Eat a whole dinner on it

effects.log: You eat a three-course dinner at {npc}'s table. Nothing slides. {npc} sits across from you and does not eat anything, too busy watching the table.

choices.text: Order a matching cabinet (8 taels)

effects.log: Your first proper order. {npc} takes it so seriously the cabinet takes four months, and is beautiful.

events.text: {npc} is a master carpenter now with a workshop and apprentices of {his} own. {He} comes to see the crooked chair, which is still in your house, and sits in it.

choices.text: Tell {npc} it never wobbled again

effects.log: {npc} lifts the leg and finds the folded paper, and laughs until the apprentices come in to see.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to make one for the next apprentice to measure against

mem.note: gave my chair to the workshop

effects.log: {npc} takes the crooked chair to the workshop. Every new apprentice is shown it, and the paper under the leg.

events.text: {npc} keeps pigeons, and has trained one to fly between {his} roof and yours, as an experiment. The pigeon arrives with a message: Does this work?

choices.text: Send the pigeon back with a reply

effects.log: You write: It works. The pigeon goes home. A second message comes within the hour: Excellent. What is for dinner?

choices.text: Keep the pigeon a day and feed it well

effects.log: The pigeon goes home a little fatter. {npc} writes that it has never flown so slowly. You both find this very funny.

events.text: The pigeon post between your roofs carries a message most days now: gossip, jokes, the price of eggs. Today the pigeon comes in fast, and the message says: Help. Roof. Now.

choices.text: Run

effects.log: {npc}'s roof has a beehive in the eaves, a large and angry one. You and {npc} move it in a bucket at dusk, both stung, both laughing.

choices.text: Send the pigeon back asking what kind of help

effects.log: The pigeon brings: BEES. You arrive with smoke and a sack. The bees move without a single sting, which {npc} considers a miracle.

events.text: The old pigeon has been retired to the coop, and a young one flies the route. {npc} sends it with a message that took {him} a long time to write: what the pigeon post has meant, all these years.

choices.text: Write a long answer and send the young pigeon back

effects.log: The young pigeon struggles with the weight. {npc} reads it on the roof and waves at you across the gap.

choices.text: Walk over and say it in person

effects.log: {npc} opens the door with the message still in {his} hand. 'You could have sent the pigeon,' {he} says, and lets you in.

events.text: Years ago, in a lean winter, you gave {npc} a sack of rice and forgot it. {npc} did not forget. Today {he} arrives with a sack of rice, and a second sack, and a third.

choices.text: Accept the rice, and give the third sack away

effects.log: You take two and carry the third to the widow at the end of the street. {npc} watches you go and nods to the street.

choices.text: Accept all three with thanks

effects.log: Three sacks of rice in your store. {npc} looks lighter than you have ever seen {him}, as if {he} has put down something heavier than rice.

events.text: Another lean winter in the district. {npc} comes to you, not to borrow, but with a plan: a rice store for the street, filled in good years, opened in bad.

choices.text: Give a sack to start it

mem.note: started the rice store with me

effects.log: The rice store starts with your sack and {npc}'s. By the end of autumn there are thirty. That winter nobody in the street goes hungry.

choices.text: Help build the store-room (6 taels)

effects.log: A dry room with a raised floor and a cat. {npc} paints a sign: The Sack of Rice. Nobody but you knows why.

events.text: The street's rice store has run for years, and the young folk who look after it now ask {npc} and you to open it on the first day of a lean winter, as founders.

choices.text: Open it, and hand out the first sack

mem.note: opened the rice store with me

effects.log: You hand the first sack to a young couple with a baby, who do not know who you are. {npc} squeezes your arm.

choices.text: Tell the young ones about the first sack

mem.note: told the story of the sack

effects.log: You tell them about the lean winter and the forgotten sack of rice. They write it on the wall of the store-room.

events.text: {npc} is getting married in a hurry, before either family can object, and needs a witness who will not panic. {He} thinks you will not panic.

choices.text: Be the witness

effects.log: The ceremony is in a borrowed temple at dawn. You do not panic. The families find out by noon, panic, and then throw a banquet.

choices.text: Talk {npc} into telling the families first

effects.log: {npc} goes pale and agrees. The families shout for a week, and then throw a banquet. {npc} says you were right, eventually.

events.text: {npc}'s first child is to be named, and {npc} wants you there. 'You did not panic,' {he} says. 'The baby should meet someone who does not panic.'

choices.text: Hold the baby, calmly

effects.log: The baby screams the whole time. You do not panic. {npc} says the baby has learned something already.

choices.text: Bring a gift for the child (4 taels)

mem.note: brought my child a silver lock

effects.log: A little silver lock on a red cord, for long life. {npc} puts it round the baby's neck at once.

events.text: {npc}'s child, grown, is getting married, in a hurry, before the families can object, and has come to you for a witness who will not panic. {npc} does not know.

choices.text: Witness it, and then tell {npc} first

effects.log: You witness it at dawn and walk straight to {npc}'s door. {npc} laughs so hard {he} has to lean on the gate, then panics, then throws a banquet.

choices.text: Send the young ones to tell {npc} themselves

mem.note: sent my child to tell me

effects.log: The young couple go, terrified. {npc} hears them out, and looks over their heads at you across the street, and starts to laugh.

events.arc: The Neighbour Who Brews Better Tea
events.text: {npc} has tasted your tea and pronounced it adequate. {He} invites you over to taste what tea should be, and spends an hour warming the pot before you are allowed to touch the cup.

choices.text: Drink it slowly and admit it is better

effects.log: It is much better. {npc} is gracious in victory, and gives you a pinch of leaves to take home, to see what you do with them.

choices.text: Invite {npc} to a return match

mem.note: challenged me to a tea match

effects.log: Next week {npc} tastes your tea, with your best leaves and your best pot. {He} says it is now nearly adequate. This is war.

events.arc: The Neighbour Who Brews Better Tea
events.text: The tea war has gone on for years. Each of you hunts the hills for better leaves and the market for better water. This spring {npc} arrives with a jar of rainwater from a temple roof, very smug.

choices.text: Brew a tea to beat temple rainwater

ok.log: You use snow melted from the plum blossoms. {npc} drinks, sits very still, and declares a truce out of respect.

mem.note: admitted defeat in the tea war

fail.log: Your tea is good, and {npc}'s is better. You admit it. {npc} says the admission is worth more than the leaves.

choices.text: Propose a joint pot, both waters

mem.note: brewed a joint pot with me

effects.log: Half rain, half well. It tastes of nothing in particular. You both laugh so much that the tea war gets a new rule: one joint pot a year.

events.arc: The Neighbour Who Brews Better Tea
events.text: {npc} is old, and {his} hands shake too much to warm the pot properly now. {He} sits you down and asks you to make the tea in {his} kitchen, with {his} things.

choices.text: Make it the way {npc} taught you

effects.log: An hour warming the pot. {npc} drinks, and nods once, the best review you have ever had.

choices.text: Make it your own way, with the plum-blossom snow

effects.log: {npc} drinks and laughs. 'Still showing off,' {he} says, and drinks another cup.

events.arc: The Coat That Took Ten Years
events.text: {npc} is a tailor, and has decided you are badly dressed. {He} measures you without asking, on the spot, in the street, and says the coat will be ready when it is ready.

choices.text: Stand still and be measured

effects.log: {npc} measures everything, twice, and writes the numbers on {his} cuff. People stop to watch. You feel very important.

choices.text: Ask what colour

effects.log: {npc} looks at you a long time. 'Not blue,' {he} says. 'Everyone thinks blue. You are a grey with a lining of red.' You have no idea what that means.

events.arc: The Coat That Took Ten Years
events.text: {npc} measures you again. And again, a year later. The coat is not ready, {he} says, because you keep changing shape.

choices.text: Promise to stop changing shape

effects.log: {npc} laughs for the first time you have seen. 'Nobody can promise that,' {he} says, and measures you anyway, gently.

choices.text: Ask to see the coat so far

effects.log: It is a grey sleeve with a red lining, and nothing else. It is the most beautiful sleeve you have ever seen.

events.arc: The Coat That Took Ten Years
events.text: Ten years after the first measuring, {npc} arrives at your door with a parcel. The coat: grey, with a lining of red. It fits as if you had been poured into it.

choices.text: Wear it at once, everywhere

effects.log: You wear it to the market, to the temple, to bed once by accident. Strangers ask who made it. You tell them.

choices.text: Pay {npc} more than asked (20 taels)

effects.log: {npc} takes it, and then gives half back, and then takes it again, and says the coat was worth more and you are both fools.

events.text: The footbridge over the stream has lost three planks, and {npc}, who uses it every day to reach a field, asks if you will help mend it before the rains.

choices.text: Mend it with {npc}

ok.log: Three new planks of good pine, pegged and tied. You both walk across it ten times to admire it.

mem.note: chased the plank down the stream

fail.log: You drop a plank into the stream and chase it a long way down. The bridge gets mended anyway, with a plank that is slightly too short.

choices.text: Pay a carpenter (5 taels)

effects.log: The carpenter does it properly in a morning. {npc} insists on paying half, in eggs, over a month.

events.text: The spring flood has taken the footbridge altogether. {npc} stands on the far bank with a field to plant and no way across.

choices.text: Build a new bridge, higher this time

mem.note: built the high bridge with me

effects.log: A week of work with {npc} and half the village. The new bridge stands on stone piers above the flood mark.

choices.text: Carry {npc} across on your back until it is built

effects.log: Every morning for a month you carry {npc} across the stream. The village laughs, then starts helping with the bridge.

events.text: The high footbridge has stood through ten floods. The village has carved a name on its post, and {npc} brings you to see it.

choices.text: Read it

mem.note: read the bridge name with me

effects.log: It says: the bridge of two fools and a flood. {npc} is very proud of it. So are you.

choices.text: Cross it together, slowly

effects.log: Halfway over, {npc} stops to look at the water, and says this is the best thing {he} ever built, and you helped.

events.arc: The Notice on the Temple Wall
events.text: {npc} has been looking for a younger sibling lost in a famine twenty years ago, and has written a notice to paste on every temple wall in the county. {He} asks you to help write it, because {his} hand is poor.

choices.text: Write the notice clearly

effects.log: You write it large: a name, an age, a scar on the left hand, a song the child used to sing. {npc} reads it back many times.

choices.text: Paste them up on your travels too

effects.log: You carry a bundle of notices and paste them on temple walls wherever you go. Every time, you say the name aloud once.

events.arc: The Notice on the Temple Wall
events.text: A letter, in an unknown hand, has come to the temple for {npc}: someone in a far town has a scar on the left hand and knows the song. {npc} is shaking too hard to read the rest.

choices.text: Read it aloud for {npc}

effects.log: It is from a dyer in the south who was taken in by strangers in the famine and was told nothing of home. The dyer remembers the song. {npc} sits down in the street.

choices.text: Offer to make the journey with {npc}

mem.note: came with me to find my sibling

effects.log: {npc} grips your arm and says yes before you have finished. You set off within the week.

events.arc: The Notice on the Temple Wall
events.text: {npc} has brought the dyer home from the south, and the two of them sit in your kitchen singing the song from the famine years, slightly differently, arguing about every line.

choices.text: Join in with the bits you know

effects.log: You know three lines from the notice. You sing them wrong. Both of them correct you at once, the same way.

choices.text: Paste one last notice: found

effects.log: You write it large on the temple wall where the first one hung: Found. People stop to read it all week.

events.text: Swallows have built a nest above the door of {npc}'s shop, and customers are getting dirty shoulders. {npc} refuses to move the nest: swallows bring luck. {He} asks what you would do.

choices.text: Build a little shelf under the nest

mem.note: built a shelf for the swallows

effects.log: A shelf to catch the mess. The customers stop complaining. The swallows seem pleased.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to move the door

mem.note: told me to move the door

effects.log: {npc} stares at you, then laughs, then actually moves the door. The shop now has a door to one side and a swallow shrine over the old one.

events.text: {npc}'s shop has done better every year since the swallows came. Now there are four nests. {npc} has started naming them and keeping a ledger of their comings and goings.

choices.text: Help keep the swallow ledger

mem.note: kept the swallow ledger with me

effects.log: Arrival date, eggs, fledglings, departure. After a few years you can tell the weather of the spring by the swallows, more or less.

choices.text: Paint a sign: The Swallow Shop

effects.log: The shop is renamed. People come from other streets for the swallows. {npc} is mortified by the success.

events.text: This spring the swallows are late, and {npc} has been standing at the door every morning, watching the sky. Today {he} sends a child running for you.

choices.text: Run, and watch them arrive

mem.note: watched the swallows come home with me

effects.log: Four swallows, then nine, then too many to count, all at once over the roofs. {npc} laughs out loud in the street and grabs your arm.

choices.text: Bring tea and wait with {npc}

mem.note: waited for the swallows with me

effects.log: You wait all morning. At noon the first swallow comes. {npc} writes the date in the ledger with a hand that shakes.

events.arc: The Worst Flute in the County
events.text: {npc} has taken up the bamboo flute, and practises in the evenings, and the dogs of the street howl along. {He} asks you, very hopefully, for your honest opinion.

choices.text: Give your honest opinion, kindly

mem.note: told me the truth about my flute

effects.log: You say it sounds like a goose in distress, but a brave goose. {npc} laughs and keeps practising, more quietly.

choices.text: Find {npc} a teacher

effects.log: An old blind flute player by the temple agrees to give lessons. The dogs of the street begin to relax.

events.arc: The Worst Flute in the County
events.text: {npc} has improved. The dogs no longer howl, only sigh. {He} wants to play at the spring fair, in front of people, and is terrified.

choices.text: Stand in the front row

effects.log: {npc} plays to you, only you, the whole piece. It is wobbly and real. The fair applauds, and {npc} looks at you, astonished.

choices.text: Play a drum beside {npc}

mem.note: drummed beside me at the fair

effects.log: You cannot play the drum. Nobody notices the flute's mistakes over your drumming. It is a triumph.

events.arc: The Worst Flute in the County
events.text: {npc} plays the flute every evening now, beautifully. The dogs of the street sit and listen. Tonight {he} plays a piece you have never heard, and says it is called The Brave Goose.

choices.text: Listen to the end

effects.log: It begins like the first evenings, wobbly and lost, and ends like now. You are not ashamed to wipe your eyes.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to teach the street's children

mem.note: had me teach the goose song

effects.log: Every child in the street learns The Brave Goose, badly. The dogs howl again. {npc} says that is how it should be.

events.text: {npc} is moving house across town with one handcart and the contents of a whole life. {He} asks you to help, and promises dumplings.

choices.text: Push the handcart

effects.log: Seven trips. On the fourth a wardrobe falls off at the bridge and the whole street helps pick it up. The dumplings are very good.

choices.text: Help {npc} decide what to leave behind

effects.log: Three broken chairs, a cracked jar, a box of letters nobody wants to read. {npc} keeps the letters. The rest stays.

events.text: {npc} has finished settling into the new house and is having a housewarming. Nobody has come yet. {He} is standing by a table of food, looking at the door.

choices.text: Go in and stay until the others come

effects.log: The others come, late and all at once. By midnight the house is warm in every sense. {npc} says you were the first, and that counts.

choices.text: Go and fetch the neighbours

effects.log: You knock on every door in the new street. By dark the house is full of strangers eating {npc}'s food. By next year they are neighbours.

events.text: {npc} has lived in the new house for many years now, and it is not new any more. {He} shows you the box of old letters from the move. {He} has decided to read them, at last, with you there.

choices.text: Read them together

mem.note: read the old letters with me

effects.log: Love letters, debts, a child's drawing. {npc} laughs at some and goes quiet at others. At the end {he} burns half and keeps half.

choices.text: Sit with {npc} while {he} reads alone

effects.log: You make tea and stay quiet. When {npc} looks up, finally, {he} just says, 'Thank you for helping me move.'

events.text: Years ago you paid {npc}'s ferry fare when {he} was a copper short, and forgot it. {npc} did not. Today {he} is waiting at the ferry with a small boat of {his} own, and says the next crossing is free, for life.

choices.text: Accept, and cross in style

effects.log: {npc} rows you over with great ceremony and a small flag. The ferryman glares from the big ferry.

choices.text: Insist on paying one copper each time

effects.log: {npc} takes the copper every time with a bow, and puts each one in a jar marked with your name.

events.text: {npc} has a second boat now, and a third. The little ferry has become a business, and the big ferryman has started to bring {npc} complaints in person.

choices.text: Broker a truce between the two ferries

effects.log: The big ferry carries carts, the little ones carry people. Both ferrymen eat noodles together on the bank to seal it.

choices.text: Help {npc} paint the new boats

effects.log: Three boats, each with a painted eye on the prow. {npc} lets you name one. You name it Copper Short.

events.text: {npc} rows you across one last time before giving the boats to a nephew. In the middle of the river {he} gives you the jar of coppers, every one you ever paid.

choices.text: Take the jar and pay the nephew from it

mem.note: paid my nephew from the jar

effects.log: You use {npc}'s jar of coppers to pay the nephew for every crossing after. {npc} hears of it and laughs for a week.

choices.text: Pour the coppers into the river, for luck

mem.note: gave the coppers to the river

effects.log: They go into the brown water in a little shower. {npc} watches them go and says that is exactly what {he} would have done.

events.text: {npc} is in love with someone in the next town and cannot write, or not well enough. {He} asks you to write the letters, and swears you to secrecy.

choices.text: Write them in {npc}'s words

mem.note: wrote my letters in my words

effects.log: You write exactly what {npc} says, clumsy and true. The answer comes in two weeks, and it is clumsy and true too.

choices.text: Write them beautifully

effects.log: Your letters are full of moon and willow. The answer is polite and puzzled: who wrote this? It does not sound like {npc}.

events.text: The person in the next town has written back to say they are coming to visit, and {npc} is in a panic, because they will want to talk about the letters.

choices.text: Teach {npc} to write, quickly

effects.log: A month of evenings. When the visitor comes, {npc} writes a note in front of them, badly, in {his} own hand. The visitor keeps it.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to confess

effects.log: {npc} confesses about the letters. The visitor laughs and says they could tell, and that they liked the clumsy bits best.

events.text: {npc} and the person from the next town are married, and have asked you, the writer of letters, to write the words on their wedding scroll.

choices.text: Write it in {npc}'s words

effects.log: One line, the clumsiest line from the first letter. Everyone at the wedding reads it. Some of them cry.

choices.text: Make {npc} write it, with your hand on {his}

effects.log: The characters come out half yours and half {npc}'s. It is the most honest scroll anyone there has seen.

events.text: {npc} keeps bees in log hives behind the house and is short of hands for the honey harvest. {He} offers you a jar of honey for a day's help, and a veil that has holes in it.

choices.text: Help with the harvest

ok.log: Not one sting. {npc} says the bees like you, and that this is rare and slightly suspicious. You go home with two jars.

fail.log: Eleven stings, mostly through the holes in the veil. {npc} rubs mud on them and gives you three jars out of guilt.

choices.text: Mend the veil first

effects.log: You stitch the holes before the harvest. {npc} is astonished that nobody thought of it before. The day goes without a sting.

events.text: {npc}'s bees have swarmed and are hanging in a great humming ball from the plum tree in your yard. {npc} arrives at a run with a basket and a look of great joy.

choices.text: Hold the basket while {npc} shakes them in

effects.log: Thousands of bees fall into the basket with a sound like rain. {npc} says you are now a beekeeper too, whether you like it or not.

choices.text: Let them stay in your plum tree and start a hive

mem.note: started a hive from my swarm

effects.log: {npc} helps you build a log hive. By autumn you have honey of your own, and an opinion about bees.

events.text: {npc} is too old to lift the log hives now, and sits in the garden in a hat with a veil, telling you what the bees are thinking while you do the lifting.

choices.text: Do exactly what {npc} says

mem.note: listened to me and the bees

effects.log: The bees do not sting you once. {npc} says it is because you listened to the bees, and to {him}, in that order.

choices.text: Bring the first jar of the year to {npc}

effects.log: {npc} opens it, smells it, and names the flowers in it, one by one, with eyes shut.

events.arc: The Salt Merchant and the Camel
events.text: On the dusty western road you meet {npc}, a salt merchant leading a camel so bad-tempered it has bitten three customs officers this month. The camel looks at you and does not bite. {npc} is amazed.

choices.text: Walk a day with {npc} and the camel

effects.log: You walk to the next town. {npc} tells you the price of salt in nine provinces and the camel's whole history of crimes. At the gate {he} gives you a twist of salt for luck.

choices.text: Buy a sack of salt (4 taels)

effects.log: {npc} gives you a fair price and a warning: never trust anyone who sells salt cheap. You sell it on in the next town for six.

events.arc: The Salt Merchant and the Camel
events.text: {npc} comes through your town with the camel and the salt, and seeks you out. The camel is ill and will not eat, and {npc}, who claims to hate it, is in despair.

choices.text: Sit up with the camel

effects.log: You sit up with the camel all night, feeding it soaked beans by hand. By dawn it bites you, which {npc} says means it is better.

choices.text: Fetch a horse doctor (3 taels)

effects.log: The horse doctor says it has eaten a rope. Out comes the rope. The camel bites the horse doctor. {npc} weeps with relief.

events.arc: The Salt Merchant and the Camel
events.text: {npc} is retiring from the salt road and has come to ask you something odd: would you keep the camel? It does not bite you, and it will not go with anyone else.

choices.text: Take the camel

effects.log: The camel moves into your yard and terrorises the hens. It never bites you. {npc} visits it every spring and says it looks fat.

choices.text: Find the camel a home at a caravan inn

effects.log: The caravan inn takes the camel as a mascot. It bites only the rude guests, which is a great service.

events.text: At a crossroads village a puppet troupe is performing on a cart, and the voice of the villain has lost a voice. {npc}, who runs the troupe, looks out at the crowd and points at you.

choices.text: Do the villain's voice

effects.log: You growl and sneer and threaten the princess. Children boo you so hard that you feel you have achieved something. {npc} offers you a job.

choices.text: Do the princess instead and swap the puppets

effects.log: Now the villain is played by the old puppeteer in a squeak, and the princess by you in a roar. It is the funniest show the village has ever seen.

events.text: The puppet cart comes through your town. {npc} has carved a new puppet, and it is clearly you: your face, your walk. It is the hero of the play now.

choices.text: Watch yourself save the princess

effects.log: Your puppet is braver and better-looking than you. The town cheers. You cheer loudest.

choices.text: Ask to work your own puppet

effects.log: You work the puppet of yourself, badly. It trips over the princess. {npc} says it is the most accurate show {he} has ever staged.

events.text: {npc} is old and the troupe is passing to a young puppeteer. At the last show, the puppet of you takes a bow, and {npc} gives it to you.

choices.text: Keep the puppet

effects.log: Your puppet hangs on your wall, braver than you, forever. Children who visit ask to make it talk. You growl.

choices.text: Give the puppet back to the young troupe

mem.note: gave the puppet to the troupe

effects.log: The young puppeteer keeps it in the play. Years later, in a far town, you see yourself save a princess again.

events.arc: The Ferry at the Edge of Nowhere
events.text: Far up a valley the road ends at a wide river and a ferry run by {npc}, who has not had a passenger in nine days and is delighted to have one. The ferry is a raft. The rope is old.

choices.text: Cross on the raft

effects.log: {npc} poles you over, talking the whole way. The rope creaks. You arrive dry and {npc} refuses the fare, because of the conversation.

choices.text: Help {npc} replace the old rope first

effects.log: You spend an afternoon braiding a new rope from hemp. {npc} tests it and nearly cries. Then you cross.

events.arc: The Ferry at the Edge of Nowhere
events.text: You come back up the valley. The river is in flood, the raft is beached, and {npc} is on the bank trying to hold a cow, a widow and a pedlar from crossing.

choices.text: Help ferry them across when the river drops

effects.log: Two days of waiting, then a long careful crossing with the cow complaining. {npc} says you should have been a ferry hand.

choices.text: Help build a better raft, with sides

effects.log: A raft with sides and a rail. The cow approves. {npc} paints it blue.

events.arc: The Ferry at the Edge of Nowhere
events.text: The valley road has a village on it now, and {npc}'s raft is a proper ferry with a roof. {npc} is old, and greets you by name from the far bank, before you are close enough to see faces.

choices.text: Cross and stay the night

effects.log: {npc} cooks river fish and tells everyone in the ferry house how you braided the rope. The rope is still there, retired, hanging on the wall.

choices.text: Take a turn at the pole

effects.log: You pole the ferry across while {npc} sits like a passenger for the first time in forty years, and complains about the steering.

events.text: Caught in snow under a high pass, you stumble into a small inn kept by {npc}, who is alone, has one pot of soup and one other guest: a goat. {npc} looks at you, at the soup and at the goat.

choices.text: Share the soup and the fire

effects.log: The soup is mostly turnip. The goat sleeps against your back. {npc} tells you about the forty winters {he} has kept the inn.

choices.text: Go out and cut firewood for the night

mem.note: cut my wood in the snow

effects.log: You cut wood until your hands ache. The inn is warm all night for the first time in a week. {npc} will not take your money.

events.text: Back under the pass in winter, you find the inn's guest book on the table, and your name in it from last time, and under it {npc} has written: came in the snow, cut the wood.

choices.text: Write a line in the book

effects.log: You write: came back. {npc} reads it and goes to fetch the good wine that {he} has been saving for no reason.

choices.text: Mend the inn's roof

effects.log: A week on the roof in the cold. The snow stops coming in over the third bed. {npc} renames the third bed after you.

events.text: {npc} is very old and the inn is to be closed; nobody will take it on. On the last night {he} asks you to keep the guest book.

choices.text: Take the book

effects.log: Forty years of names and the weather. You read it on long nights. Sometimes you write a line in it yourself, about the snow where you are.

choices.text: Find someone to keep the inn (15 taels)

effects.log: A young couple from the valley take it on with your silver for the first winter's stores. {npc} stays on as the old one who knows everything.

events.text: In a market town {npc} is selling a cure-all from a cart: one tonic for coughs, baldness, broken hearts and bad luck. The crowd is buying. You can smell that it is mostly vinegar.

choices.text: Say so, loudly

effects.log: The crowd turns. {npc} leaves town in a hurry, but not before giving you a very long look.

choices.text: Buy a bottle and talk to {npc} afterwards

mem.note: talked to me after the show

effects.log: {npc} admits it is vinegar and honey, and that {he} would sell real medicine if {he} knew any. {He} seems tired.

events.text: {npc} is back in town, with a new sign: Honest Remedies. {He} has spent a year with a herbalist in the hills and wants you to test {his} cough syrup, since you know what vinegar smells like.

choices.text: Test it

effects.log: It is real: loquat, honey, a little ginger. Your cough of a month stops in two days. You tell the market, loudly.

choices.text: Bring {npc} to the town physician

effects.log: The physician tests the syrup, grunts, and offers to send {npc} customers. {npc} stands there with an open mouth.

events.text: {npc} runs a proper herb shop now, with an apprentice and a reputation. On the wall, framed, is the first bottle of vinegar tonic, with a label that says: Never Again.

choices.text: Buy a bottle of the vinegar for old times (1 tael)

effects.log: {npc} sells it to you with great solemnity. It is the only one {he} still makes. You drink it on the step and both of you laugh.

choices.text: Send the sick of your street to {npc}

mem.note: sent me the sick of their street

effects.log: {npc} cures half of them and is honest with the rest. The street trusts {him} completely.

events.text: On a lonely stretch of the imperial road a post rider's horse has gone lame, and {npc}, the rider, is sitting on a milestone with a bag of letters and a look of doom. The next station is twenty li.

choices.text: Carry the letter bag to the station

effects.log: Twenty li with a bag of other people's news. At the station they make {npc} walk the horse in later, and give you tea.

choices.text: Lead the lame horse while {npc} runs ahead

effects.log: {npc} runs the letters in, and you walk the horse. The station master praises you both and fines {npc} anyway.

events.text: A letter arrives for you, delivered with great ceremony by {npc} in person, who has transferred to your district. It is only a bill. {npc} is embarrassed.

choices.text: Laugh, and give {npc} a cup of tea

mem.note: gave me tea at the door

effects.log: {npc} drinks it on your step and tells you which houses get love letters and which get bills. You are sworn to secrecy.

choices.text: Write {npc} a letter to deliver to {him}self

effects.log: You post a letter to {npc}. {npc} delivers it to the rider, reads it in the street, and laughs out loud.

events.text: {npc}'s last day as a post rider. {He} has asked to deliver your post on the last round, whatever it is, and it turns out to be a letter you have been waiting years for.

choices.text: Open it on the step with {npc} there

mem.note: opened the last letter with me

effects.log: It is good news. {npc} says {he} always knew which letters were good, by the weight. You do not believe it, and you do.

choices.text: Give {npc} a parting gift: new riding boots (6 taels)

effects.log: {npc} puts them on at once and says that now {he} will have to keep riding, just for the boots.

events.arc: A Stretch of the Tea Horse Road
events.text: On the high road you fall in with a mule caravan carrying tea bricks over the mountains, led by {npc}, who is short a hand and offers you a mule and meals for a week's walking.

choices.text: Join the caravan for a week

mem.note: walked the tea road with me

effects.log: A week of mountain paths, bells on the mules and terrible jokes by the fire. The mule you lead is called Grandmother and is the cleverest beast you have ever met.

choices.text: Decline, but share their fire one night

effects.log: One night of jokes and butter tea. In the morning {npc} gives you a brick of tea wrapped in bamboo for the road.

events.arc: A Stretch of the Tea Horse Road
events.text: The tea caravan winds into your town, bells and all, and {npc} comes to find you. Grandmother the mule has asked for you, {npc} says, by refusing to move until you are fetched.

choices.text: Go and talk to Grandmother

effects.log: Grandmother looks at you, sniffs you, and walks on. {npc} says that is the warmest welcome {he} has ever seen the mule give.

choices.text: Walk with the caravan to the next town

effects.log: Two days on the road with old friends. {npc} tells everyone you are the best mule hand the caravan never had.

events.arc: A Stretch of the Tea Horse Road
events.text: {npc} brings the caravan through one last time; the young ones will lead it now. Grandmother the mule is retiring too, and {npc} asks if Grandmother may retire to your yard.

choices.text: Give Grandmother a home

effects.log: Grandmother moves in, eats your garden and outlives two neighbours' horses. {npc} visits twice a year with tea.

choices.text: Buy the old mule a field by the river (8 taels)

effects.log: Grandmother gets a field to graze. {npc} cries a little, and blames the dust.

events.text: At a roadside tea stall {npc}, a storyteller with a clapper and a fan, is telling the tale of a hero who never existed, and getting the details wrong in a way that is very entertaining.

choices.text: Listen to the end and pay a copper

effects.log: The hero dies, is reborn, marries a dragon and opens a noodle shop. You pay two coppers. {npc} bows.

choices.text: Tell {npc} a true story from your own road

effects.log: {npc} listens to the whole thing with narrowed eyes, and says {he} will improve it.

events.text: In a teahouse in your town a crowd is listening to {npc}, the crossroads storyteller. The story is about you. It is vastly improved. You fought eleven bandits and a tiger.

choices.text: Sit at the back and enjoy it

effects.log: You are magnificent in the story. The crowd adores you. Nobody looks at you twice.

choices.text: Correct {npc} from the back

effects.log: 'It was one bandit,' you say. The crowd turns. {npc} says, without missing a beat, 'And here is the hero, too modest to admit the tiger.' Everyone cheers.

events.text: {npc} is old and has come to ask you for the true ending of your story. {He} has told it for years and would like, just once, to tell it right.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the whole truth

effects.log: {npc} listens, nods, and tells it in the teahouse that night, the true version. It is quieter and better. The crowd is silent at the end.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to keep the tiger

effects.log: {npc} laughs until {he} coughs. 'The tiger stays,' {he} says. The tiger stays.

events.text: At a crossroads a blind erhu player, {npc}, is playing for coppers in the rain, and nobody is stopping. The music is very good and very sad.

choices.text: Stop, listen and lead {npc} to shelter

mem.note: led me out of the rain

effects.log: You take {npc}'s arm to the eaves of a shrine. {He} plays you a happy song there, out of thanks, and it turns out {he} knows a great many.

choices.text: Drop silver in the bowl (3 taels)

effects.log: {npc} hears the weight and stops playing. 'That is too much,' {he} says, and plays your favourite song without being told it.

events.text: {npc} plays at the corner by your market now. When you pass, {he} switches to the happy song from the shrine, every time, without fail. {He} says you walk like nobody else.

choices.text: Sing along one morning

effects.log: You sing badly. The market stops and listens, and then the market sings too. {npc}'s bowl is full by noon.

choices.text: Bring {npc} a new bow for the erhu (4 taels)

effects.log: Horsehair and bamboo. {npc} tightens it, plays one note, and turns {his} face up to the sun.

events.text: {npc} is teaching a child to play the erhu at the market corner, by touch. When you pass, the child plays the happy song from the shrine, badly. {npc} is beaming.

choices.text: Stop and listen to the whole song

effects.log: It takes three tries. {npc} says the child will be better than {him}. You think {npc} is right.

choices.text: Pay for the child's own erhu (5 taels)

effects.log: The child gets an erhu of their own. {npc} runs fingers over it and names the wood.

events.text: On a hill above a nameless valley, {npc} is mapping the county with a string, a compass and enormous patience, and needs someone to hold the far end of the string.

choices.text: Hold the string all day

effects.log: You stand on hilltops while {npc} shouts numbers across the valley. By dusk the valley exists on paper, and the hill you stood on has your name.

choices.text: Ask what the hill is called

effects.log: 'Nothing,' says {npc}. 'Nobody ever asked.' {He} lets you name it. You name it something silly. It goes on the map.

events.text: A copy of {npc}'s county map has reached your town and is pinned up in the magistrate's yard. There, on a hill above a nameless valley, is the silly name.

choices.text: Show everyone

effects.log: Half the town walks out to see the hill. It is a very ordinary hill. Everyone is delighted with it.

choices.text: Write to {npc} with a correction

effects.log: There is a stream {npc} missed. {npc} writes back with thanks, and a new copy with the stream on it, named after you as well.

events.text: {npc} visits, old, with the last map of {his} life: the whole province. {He} wants you to walk up the silly hill with {him} one more time.

choices.text: Walk up the hill together

mem.note: walked up our hill with me

effects.log: At the top {npc} unrolls the province on the grass. Your hill is on it, still silly. {npc} sits on it and looks at it for a long time.

choices.text: Carry the string to the far hill

mem.note: held the string one last time

effects.log: You stand on the far hill one last time and {npc} shouts numbers across the valley, which has not moved at all.

events.text: A travelling bird seller, {npc}, has a pole hung with bamboo cages full of larks and finches. One small brown bird in a cage at the end has not sung once, and {npc} says it is worthless.

choices.text: Buy the silent bird and let it go (2 taels)

effects.log: You open the cage on the hillside. The bird sits on your finger, then on a branch, and sings like a waterfall. {npc} stares.

choices.text: Ask why {npc} sells birds at all

effects.log: {npc} shrugs: it is what {his} father did. Then {he} looks at the pole of cages for a long time.

events.text: {npc} finds you in your town. The pole is lighter: {he} has been opening cages on hillsides, one bird a week, and now has hardly any to sell, and no idea how to live.

choices.text: Help {npc} find honest work with birds

effects.log: The temple wants someone to keep its pigeons and its old crane. {npc} is perfect for it.

choices.text: Lend {npc} silver to start again (8 taels)

mem.note: lent me silver to start again

effects.log: {npc} starts a stall selling bird feed and nests. Free birds come to eat. It is somehow a better business.

events.text: At {npc}'s stall the roof is crowded with wild birds every morning. {npc} has kept one cage: the first one, the silent bird's, door open, with a nest in it.

choices.text: Sit with {npc} and listen to the morning birds

mem.note: listened to the free birds with me

effects.log: Larks, finches and one small brown bird singing like a waterfall. {npc} says it is the silent one's grandchild.

choices.text: Hang the open cage in your own yard

effects.log: {npc} gives it to you. By spring there is a nest in it, and a song.

events.arc: The Pilgrim on the Long Road
events.text: On a dusty road you overtake {npc}, a pilgrim monk walking to a temple a thousand li away, bowing to the ground every third step. {He} has been doing it for a year and is a very long way from there.

choices.text: Carry water for {npc} for a day

effects.log: You walk beside {npc} all day, three steps and a bow, carrying the water gourd. In the evening {he} blesses you, very formally, and laughs.

choices.text: Give {npc} a pair of knee pads you sew from your coat

effects.log: {npc} looks at the pads, at you, and puts them on. 'The rule says nothing against knees,' {he} says.

events.arc: The Pilgrim on the Long Road
events.text: Years later a monk knocks on your gate. It is {npc}, brown and thin, on the way home. {He} reached the temple, {he} says, and the knee pads did too, and {he} has brought you something from it.

choices.text: Accept the gift

effects.log: A small bell from the temple's own eaves. Its sound is very clear. When the wind moves it, you think of a road a thousand li long.

choices.text: Ask what was at the end of the road

mem.note: asked about the end of the road

effects.log: {npc} thinks for a long time. 'A temple,' {he} says. 'And a cup of tea, and the road home.' {He} looks very happy.

events.arc: The Pilgrim on the Long Road
events.text: {npc} has become the abbot of a small temple in the hills near you, and has asked you to walk the last three li to it with {him}, three steps and a bow, for old times.

choices.text: Walk and bow the whole way

mem.note: walked the last li with me

effects.log: Three li, three steps and a bow, in the dust. At the gate {npc} pours you a cup of tea, and you understand about the end of the road.

choices.text: Carry the water gourd beside {npc} again

effects.log: You walk beside {npc} with the gourd, as you did on the dusty road. {npc} laughs at every bow.

events.text: You take a wrong turn and come down into a valley where every house has a kiln. {npc}, a potter with clay to the elbows, offers you a bowl of water in a cup {he} made that morning.

choices.text: Ask to try the wheel

effects.log: Your first bowl collapses into a flat thing. {npc} fires it anyway and calls it a plate. You carry it home wrapped in straw.

choices.text: Buy a set of bowls (5 taels)

effects.log: Six bowls with a glaze like river water. {npc} wraps them in straw and tells you the road back, which you lose anyway.

events.text: A cart of pots arrives at your market, and with it {npc}, who has decided to sell in the town for the first time and is terrified of everyone.

choices.text: Stand at the stall with {npc} all day

effects.log: You talk to the customers; {npc} talks to the pots. By evening every pot is sold.

choices.text: Take {npc} round the shops that might buy

effects.log: Two teahouses and a noodle shop order bowls by the hundred. {npc} has to sit down on a step.

events.text: {npc} sends a parcel from the valley: one bowl, perfectly made, with a glaze like river water. In the bottom, pressed into the clay, is your flat plate's shape, copied exactly.

choices.text: Eat from it every day

effects.log: It is the best bowl you own. Its bottom is your first terrible plate. You think that is about right.

choices.text: Go back to the valley to thank {npc}

mem.note: came back by the wrong turn

effects.log: You lose the road, as always, and arrive by the wrong turn. {npc} says that is the only way anyone ever arrives.

events.text: At a horse fair {npc}, a trader with a cheerful face and no teeth, is trying to sell a mare that kicks everyone. {He} offers the mare to you for almost nothing, because {he} is tired of being kicked.

choices.text: Buy the mare (6 taels)

effects.log: The mare kicks you on the first day, and on the second, and on the tenth day lets you ride. By spring the mare is the fastest horse in the district.

choices.text: Look at the mare's feet first

effects.log: A stone bruise in the left hind hoof. You show {npc}. {He} is astonished, and gives you a cup of tea for the advice.

events.text: {npc} is at the horse fair again, and comes looking for you to ask your opinion on horses now, before {he} buys them. {He} calls it consulting.

choices.text: Consult for a share

effects.log: You find two lame horses, a liar, and one excellent pony. {npc} makes a fortune and gives you a tenth.

choices.text: Teach {npc} to look at feet

effects.log: {npc} learns quickly and is very proud of it. {He} makes everyone at the fair lift their horses' feet for {him}.

events.text: {npc} has retired from the horse fairs and sends you a message: the foal of a foal of the kicking mare is for sale, and {npc} is keeping it for you, and it kicks.

choices.text: Go and see the foal

effects.log: It kicks you at once. {npc} laughs until {he} cries. You buy it, of course.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to keep it and ride it

mem.note: gave me the foal to ride

effects.log: {npc} is old for riding. {He} rides it anyway, slowly, round the field, very proud, and is kicked only once.

events.text: A travelling opera troupe is stranded at a mountain temple by a week of rain, and {npc}, its leader, is rehearsing a battle scene in the temple hall to keep everyone from despair.

choices.text: Join the battle as a soldier

mem.note: died eleven times in my play

effects.log: You fall dead eleven times with great feeling. {npc} says you have a gift for dying.

choices.text: Help the troupe with food

mem.note: fed my troupe in the rain

effects.log: You go down the mountain in the rain for rice and cabbage. The troupe eats and sings and calls you their patron.

events.text: The opera troupe is performing in your town, and {npc} has kept a part for you: a soldier who falls dead in the second act. It is your old part.

choices.text: Fall dead in front of the whole town

effects.log: You fall magnificently. The town applauds the corpse. {npc} says it is the best death of the season.

choices.text: Ask for a speaking part this time

mem.note: got a line in my play

effects.log: You get one line: My lord, the enemy is here. You say it to a roaring crowd, then fall dead anyway.

events.text: {npc} is giving up the stage, and the troupe's last performance is a play {he} has written about a week of rain in a mountain temple. There is a character in it who falls dead eleven times.

choices.text: Watch from the front row

effects.log: The character is you, with your walk. The crowd laughs at every death. At the end, {npc} bows to you from the stage.

choices.text: Play yourself one last time

mem.note: played themselves in my last play

effects.log: {npc} insists. You fall dead eleven times in the last performance. The applause goes on for a long time.

events.arc: The Herb Gatherer on the Cliff
events.text: Climbing in the hills, you find {npc}, an old herb gatherer, hanging on a rope halfway down a cliff, unable to climb up or down because the rope has snagged.

choices.text: Free the rope from the top

ok.log: You haul {npc} up hand over hand. At the top {he} shows you the root {he} was after, worth the risk, {he} says. You disagree.

fail.log: You free it, but the rope burns your hands. {npc} climbs up the rest of the way and binds your hands with leaves from {his} bag.

choices.text: Climb down and guide {npc} by another way

effects.log: A slow traverse along a ledge. You reach the bottom together. {npc} says nobody has found that ledge in forty years.

events.arc: The Herb Gatherer on the Cliff
events.text: You find {npc} in the hills again, at the same cliff, with a new rope. {He} wants a partner at the top, and offers to teach you every herb on the mountain in return.

choices.text: Be the partner for a season

mem.note: held my rope for a season

effects.log: A season of ropes and roots. You learn thirty herbs by smell. {npc} says you will never get rich from it, and that is the point.

choices.text: Learn just the one root that saved the trip

effects.log: {npc} shows you the root, how to find it, how to dry it. It sells for a great deal in the town.

events.arc: The Herb Gatherer on the Cliff
events.text: {npc} is too old for the cliffs now. {He} gives you the rope, the bag, and the map of the mountain in {his} head, which takes an afternoon to tell.

choices.text: Climb for the root once, for {npc}

effects.log: You come back with it at dusk. {npc} smells it, and smiles, and puts it in your hand again. 'Sell it,' {he} says. 'Buy rope.'

choices.text: Write down the mountain map as {npc} tells it

effects.log: Every cliff, every root, every ledge nobody has found in forty years. You keep it in the bag with the rope.

events.arc: The Noodle Stall on the Pass
events.text: At the top of a lonely pass there is a noodle stall, and the cook, {npc}, has a scar, a very large cleaver and the manner of someone who used to rob travellers here. The noodles are excellent.

choices.text: Eat and say nothing

effects.log: The best noodles you have ever had. {npc} watches you eat with an expert's eye and gives you a second bowl free.

choices.text: Ask {npc} straight out

effects.log: {npc} puts the cleaver down. Yes, {he} used to rob travellers. Then {he} found that feeding them pays better and nobody chases you.

events.arc: The Noodle Stall on the Pass
events.text: On the pass again, you find {npc} standing between the stall and three young bandits who want the takings. {npc} is holding the cleaver and a ladle.

choices.text: Stand with {npc}

mem.note: stood with me on the pass

ok.log: The three look at the two of you and decide on noodles instead. {npc} serves them, and lectures them on career prospects.

mem.note: fought beside me on the pass

fail.log: One of them swings. You both end up bruised, and the three run off with nothing but a ladle-shaped dent each.

choices.text: Offer the bandits a job at the stall

effects.log: {npc} stares at you. The young bandits stare at you. By autumn one of them is chopping spring onions and is very happy.

events.arc: The Noodle Stall on the Pass
events.text: The noodle stall on the pass is a small inn now, and the young former bandit runs it. {npc} sits on a stool in the sun with the cleaver on {his} knee and greets you like an old comrade.

choices.text: Eat a bowl together and talk about the old days

mem.note: ate with me on the pass

effects.log: {npc} tells you about robbing travellers; you tell {him} about being one. The young cook brings bowls until you both refuse.

choices.text: Ask for the noodle secret

effects.log: {npc} whispers it: a pinch of the pepper from the far valley, and never let anyone rush you. You think it is good advice for most things.

events.arc: The Scholar Walking to the Exam
events.text: On the road to the capital you meet {npc}, a scholar walking to the imperial exams with one pair of straw sandals, one book and no money at all. {He} is reciting the classics to keep {his} mind off {his} feet.

choices.text: Share your food on the road

effects.log: {npc} eats as if it is the first meal in days, which it is, and recites a poem about rice in your honour.

choices.text: Buy {npc} a pair of cloth shoes (3 taels)

mem.note: bought me shoes for the exams

effects.log: {npc} puts them on and walks in a small circle, astonished, like a child.

events.arc: The Scholar Walking to the Exam
events.text: A letter, in beautiful brushwork: {npc} has passed the exams and has been made a county magistrate, and has not forgotten the road.

choices.text: Write back with congratulations, and a warning

effects.log: You write: be a good magistrate, or I will come and take back the shoes. {npc} writes that {he} has them framed.

choices.text: Visit {npc}'s county

effects.log: The yamen is clean, the clerks are polite, the prisoners are fed. {npc} gives you a tour and is very nervous about your opinion.

events.arc: The Scholar Walking to the Exam
events.text: {npc} has risen to be a prefect, grey now, and has come to your door in plain clothes, alone, to say that every year {he} has bought a pair of shoes for a poor scholar on the road, because of you.

choices.text: Ask how many pairs

effects.log: 'Thirty-one,' says {npc}. 'Nine of them passed.' You both sit with that a while.

choices.text: Walk a stretch of the capital road with {npc}

mem.note: walked the capital road with me

effects.log: Two old people on the road, looking out for scholars. You find one before noon, with straw sandals.

events.arc: The Fortune Teller Who Is Always Wrong
events.text: A roadside fortune teller, {npc}, reads your face and predicts with great certainty that you will marry a fisherman's child, lose a tooth to a donkey and become a minister. All before the spring.

choices.text: Pay and thank {npc} gravely (1 tael)

effects.log: None of it happens. It is a very restful spring.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to read {his} own face

mem.note: asked me to read my own face

effects.log: {npc} looks in a bowl of water and predicts great wealth. {He} has a hole in {his} shoe. You both laugh.

events.arc: The Fortune Teller Who Is Always Wrong
events.text: {npc} is on the road again, and has become famous for being wrong. People pay to hear what will not happen, and plan around it. {He} reads your face for free, for old times.

choices.text: Do the opposite of everything {npc} says

effects.log: {npc} says avoid the east road. You take the east road and find a purse of silver in a ditch. {npc} is very proud.

choices.text: Help {npc} paint a new sign

effects.log: You paint: Fortunes. Guaranteed Wrong. {npc} doubles {his} prices.

events.arc: The Fortune Teller Who Is Always Wrong
events.text: {npc} reads your face one last time, an old fortune teller retiring from the road. {He} looks a long time, and says, very quietly, that you will be happy. Then {he} looks worried.

choices.text: Laugh

effects.log: {npc} laughs too. 'I must be getting it right at last,' {he} says. 'Time to stop.'

choices.text: Tell {npc} you will be careful anyway

effects.log: {npc} nods. 'Be careful of happiness,' {he} says, 'it has a terrible sense of humour.'

events.text: At a little bridge on a back road, the toll keeper, {npc}, does not want coins. The toll is a riddle. Answer it and you cross. Fail and you go round by the ford, which is a day.

choices.text: Answer the riddle

ok.log: What has a neck and no head? A bottle. {npc} lifts the bar and bows. 'Rare,' {he} says.

fail.log: You get it wrong. {npc} sighs and points at the ford. It is a long, wet day.

choices.text: Offer {npc} a riddle instead of an answer

effects.log: {npc} considers your riddle for a full hour and then lets you across, frowning, still thinking.

events.text: The back-road bridge again. {npc} has been saving a riddle for you for a year, and has written it on a board. Other travellers are waiting to see.

choices.text: Answer it in front of everyone

ok.log: You get it. The travellers cheer. {npc} lifts the bar for everyone, free, for the rest of the day.

fail.log: You fail. Everyone goes round by the ford together, and by the end of the day you are all friends.

choices.text: Help the waiting travellers instead

effects.log: You whisper hints to an old woman with a basket. The old traveller gets it. {npc} sees exactly what you did, and lets you both through.

events.text: {npc} is old, and the bridge is to be rebuilt in stone, with a proper coin toll. {He} asks you to come for the last day of riddles.

choices.text: Ask every traveller a riddle yourself

mem.note: kept my bridge for a day

effects.log: You keep the bridge for the last day while {npc} watches. You are a cruel keeper. {npc} is very proud.

choices.text: Carve {npc}'s best riddle on the new stone

effects.log: The new bridge has a riddle carved on its parapet. People stop and argue over it for years. {npc} says that is a toll of a kind.

events.text: Down a side road you find an apricot orchard heavy with fruit and only one person picking it: {npc}, the keeper, who is in despair. The pickers have all gone to the city.

choices.text: Pick until dark

effects.log: You fill forty baskets. {npc} feeds you apricots, apricot soup and apricot tea, and gives you a basket to carry away.

choices.text: Fetch help from the nearest village

mem.note: brought the village to my orchard

effects.log: Half the village comes for a share. The orchard is picked in two days. {npc} has never been so tired or so happy.

events.text: A cart of dried apricots arrives at your door, with a note from {npc}: harvest is next month, and there is a basket with your name on it, if you come and fill it.

choices.text: Go for the harvest

effects.log: It becomes a week every year: picking in the orchard with {npc} and whoever comes. You learn which tree is sweetest and why.

choices.text: Send a letter and silver for pickers (5 taels)

effects.log: {npc} hires two pickers with it, and names a tree after you. It is the sour one, as a joke.

events.text: {npc} is too old to climb the ladders. At harvest you find {him} sitting under the sweetest tree, directing a crowd of pickers, many of whom first came because of you.

choices.text: Climb the sweetest tree and pick for {npc}

mem.note: picked the first apricot for me

effects.log: You hand {npc} the first apricot of the year, warm from the sun. {He} eats it and declares the harvest open.

choices.text: Plant a new tree beside the old one

mem.note: planted a tree in my orchard

effects.log: A sapling beside the sweetest tree. {npc} says {he} will not see it fruit. You say that is not the point. {npc} agrees.

events.text: On a mountain road far from any water you meet {npc}, an old sailor carrying an oar over one shoulder. {He} is walking inland until someone asks what the oar is. There, {he} will settle.

choices.text: Ask what it is

effects.log: {npc} stops dead and looks around. 'Here?' {he} says, dismayed. It is a goat path. You both laugh, and {he} walks on.

choices.text: Pretend you know it is an oar

effects.log: {npc} nods, approving, and walks on. 'Not yet,' {he} says. 'Not yet.'

events.text: A letter, scrawled, from a village in the hills: {npc} has found the place. A child asked what the oar was, and {npc} cried, and bought a house.

choices.text: Visit the village

mem.note: came to see where I settled

effects.log: {npc}'s house has the oar over the door. The village thinks it is a strange spade. {npc} tells them about the sea every evening, and they do not believe a word.

choices.text: Send {npc} a jar of seawater

effects.log: It takes months to arrive. {npc} writes that {he} smelled it and slept for a day and a night.

events.text: {npc} is very old. In the hill village {he} has taught the children to row, on a pond, with the oar. {He} wants you to come and see the regatta.

choices.text: Watch the pond regatta

effects.log: Three tubs, nine children, one oar passed between them. {npc} judges from a chair and everyone wins.

choices.text: Row a tub yourself

effects.log: You row a tub round the pond with {npc} shouting sea words at you. You come last. {npc} says you have a sailor's heart and a farmer's arms.

events.arc: The Charcoal Burner in the Forest
events.text: Deep in a winter forest you smell smoke and find {npc}, a charcoal burner, tending a smoking mound alone. {He} has not spoken to anyone in a month and is not sure {he} remembers how.

choices.text: Sit by the mound and talk

effects.log: {npc} speaks slowly at first, then all at once, about the trees, the foxes, the way the mound breathes. You stay until dark.

choices.text: Help rake the mound

effects.log: You work in silence until the burn is done. {npc} gives you a sack of charcoal and the first smile you have seen in the forest.

events.arc: The Charcoal Burner in the Forest
events.text: Back in the forest in winter, you find {npc}'s mound, cold, and {npc} in the hut with a fever and no one for ten li.

choices.text: Nurse {npc} through it

effects.log: Three days of broth and wet cloths. {npc} recovers and insists on giving you all the charcoal in the forest, more or less.

choices.text: Carry {npc} to the nearest village

mem.note: carried me out of the forest

effects.log: Ten li in the snow with a feverish charcoal burner on your back. The village physician sees to {npc}. You sleep for a day.

events.arc: The Charcoal Burner in the Forest
events.text: {npc} has come out of the forest for good, and lives in the village now, and talks to everyone, too much, about the foxes. {He} says it is your fault.

choices.text: Go back to the forest with {npc} for a day

mem.note: went back to the forest with me

effects.log: You sit by a cold mound site in the snow. {npc} says {he} does not miss it, and stays until dark.

choices.text: Listen to all the fox stories

effects.log: There are many. You hear all of them. {npc} is happier than you have ever seen anyone.

events.text: A tinker, {npc}, sets up under a tree in the village square and mends pots for half the price of the smith, singing. Your pot has had a hole in it for a year.

choices.text: Have the pot mended (1 tael)

effects.log: {npc} mends it in ten minutes and shows you how, with a rivet and a little tin. 'Next time, you do it,' {he} says.

choices.text: Watch {npc} work all afternoon

effects.log: Kettles, pans, a lantern, a child's bell. By the end you could almost do it. {npc} gives you a rivet as a diploma.

events.text: {npc} comes through the village again, and this time you have a pot of your own you have mended, badly. {He} inspects it like a teacher with an exam paper.

choices.text: Take the criticism

effects.log: Too much tin, rivet crooked. {npc} redoes it slowly in front of you, and you do the next one, and it is good.

choices.text: Mend a pot for {npc}, as a test

effects.log: You mend {npc}'s own kettle. {He} pours water through it, waits, and finds no leak. {He} shakes your hand.

events.text: {npc} is too old for the road and has come to sell the tinker's kit, and wants it to go to you.

choices.text: Take the kit and mend for the street

effects.log: You mend pots for the whole street for half the smith's price, singing badly. The smith complains to {npc}, who is delighted.

choices.text: Pay {npc} a fair price for it (8 taels)

effects.log: {npc} protests, then takes it. Then {he} comes round every week to see how you are using the kit, and to criticise.

events.text: {npc} has been asked to cook a wedding banquet for a hundred guests, and has said yes, and has never cooked for more than six. {He} is at your door at dawn, holding a cleaver and a list.

choices.text: Chop for a whole day

effects.log: Two hundred spring onions, forty ducks, a mountain of ginger. The banquet is a triumph. {npc} falls asleep standing up.

choices.text: Organise the kitchen like an army

effects.log: You set stations, times and a runner. {npc} cooks; you command. Every dish goes out hot. {npc} calls you general.

events.text: {npc} has become the cook the whole district hires for weddings, and has a problem: two weddings on the same day, at opposite ends of town.
